figures.caption: Figure 1: Feature quality and sample efficiency on Gemma-2-2B activations. a,c: Training dynamics at 524k width. b,d: Final performance across dictionary widths. Details in section 5.

Figure 2: Heatmaps show sprinkler probabilities under exact inference, converged BeFOND with a fixed prior, and a numerically optimized single-projection encoder. The marked observations have identical lawn wetness but different roof evidence: neutral (white, halfway dry / wet) or wet (blue). Fixed-prior inference and encoder fitting are detailed in section C.2.3.
Figure 3: BeFOND maintains the highest recovery, and without dead latents (K = 4,096). Means and 95% confidence intervals over 3 seeds. Exact values are reported in section C.3.1 and Table 4.

Figure 4: BeFOND outperforms all evaluated baselines on dictionary recover (MCC) and feature detection (Macro F1, Rare F1) in SynthSAEBench (d = 768, K = K⋆ = 16,384). Rare F1 covers the least frequent quarter of features. Bars show means over 3 initialization seeds with 95% confidence intervals, evaluated on 106 held-out samples. Table 5 gives individual-seed results.

Figure 5: Online inference with a rolling prior. The learned initial prior initializes the first belief. Under identity state dynamics, prediction carries each posterior into the next reference (green arrows). The observation model is shown by black arrows and inference by red dashed arrows. The fixed-input case presents the same observation at each step.
Table 2: SynthSAEBench training settings. Decoder and prior examples are counted separately. Full-width runs use d = 768, K = K⋆ = 16,384; superposition runs use K = 4,096.

Table 4: Individual-seed results for Figure 3 (K = 4,096, K⋆ = 16,384). MCC values retain the recorded precision. Dead latents are counted on 106 held-out examples using each model’s native activity rule (ri > 0.5 for BeFOND and Mean-field + Adam).

Figure 8: Sparsity and recovery versus β on SynthSAEBench (d = 768, K = 4,096, K⋆ = 16,384). Colors indicate the mean initial-prior cap, lines show the mean over two seeds, and shading shows their range. Each fit uses 12,000 updates and is evaluated on 8,192 examples after 5,000 inference steps.

Figure 9: BeFOND retains the highest MCC, Macro F1, and Rare F1 after baseline modifications aimed at preventing inactive features. Hatched bars denote modified recipes (d = 768, K = K⋆ = 16,384, seed 0); numerical results appear in Table 5.

Table 5: Full-width SynthSAEBench results (d = 768, K = K⋆ = 16,384). Individual rows report initialization seeds 0–2; mean rows give pointwise 95% Student-t confidence intervals for the three recovery metrics, as in Figure 4. Each evaluation uses 106 held-out examples. L0 and dead counts in mean rows are arithmetic means. The lower block retains the modified recipes (+) and continuous-run checkpoint, each at seed 0. The BeFOND runs use 181.82M decoder-update plus 18.18M prior examples.

Figure 12: Performance as a function of inference depth. Sparse probing top-1 accuracy (left), top-5 accuracy (middle), and RAVEL disentanglement (right) for BeFOND on Gemma-2-2B layer-12 activations, evaluated over T = 1, . . . , 40 inference steps at dictionary widths of 16k, 65k, 131k, and 524k. All evaluations use checkpoint 12,207, corresponding to 49,999,872 training tokens. Lines show means and shaded regions indicate ±1 sample standard deviation across three training seeds. Sparse probing peaks within the first few steps, whereas RAVEL generally benefits from longer inference.
Table 7: Gemma training and evaluation settings. Preprocessing, checkpoint, inference depth, and readout identify an evaluation configuration.

Table 8: SAEBench results for SAEs trained on 50M tokens of whitened Gemma-2-2B layer-12 activations. Entries report mean ± sample standard deviation over five training seeds (1–5), evaluated at the final checkpoint (49,999,872 tokens). Sparse-probing metrics are macro-averaged over 113 tasks; RAVEL overall is the disentanglement score. All scores are fractions, and higher is better. L0 denotes target training sparsity, fixed using a separate seed-0 pilot. Bold indicates the highest mean across L0 values within each width–architecture group, selected before rounding.
Table 9: SAEBench evaluations of released Gemma Scope layer-12 checkpoints (Lieberum et al., 2024; Karvonen et al., 2025), organized by dictionary width and average sparsity L0.
